# Welcome {.unnumbered}

::: {.audience}
For everyone
:::

Jholok helps a jewellery shop know what it has. It keeps a list of your
products, records every piece that comes in or goes out, and helps you count
what is really on the shelves, so you can see what is missing before it costs
you.

This guide is for anyone using Jholok for the first time: the shop's owner,
the people who approve counts, and the staff who count. You don't need to know
anything about accounting. Each idea is explained the first time it appears,
and every word is in the [Glossary](chapters/glossary.qmd).

::: {.callout-note}
## This guide is being written

The chapters are being added one by one. Chapters that are not ready yet say
so.
:::

## How this guide is arranged

- **The ideas behind the app** explains stock, the ledger and counting in plain
  words. Read this part first, even if you only count.
- **Everyday use** sets the shop up and keeps the catalogue and stock up to
  date.
- **Counting** walks through a count, from opening it to counting boxes of
  pieces.
- **Checking a count** is for the owner and the people who approve counts.
- **Looking after your shop** covers backups and privacy, and ends with stories
  from a shop's year.

Each chapter says who it is for, starts with what you'll learn and ends with
what to remember.

## The shop in this guide

Every example and picture uses the same made-up shop, **Jholok Jewellers**,
with its owner Bidisha and staff Sita, Ramesh and Meena. It is the same shop
that the app's demo shows, so what you read here matches what you see on the
screen. None of its stock is real.

## Which app this guide describes

This is guide 0.1, for Jholok 0.1. The [What changed](chapters/what-changed.qmd)
page lists what is new in each edition of the guide.
